clue.text: Pressing demand from internet pioneer for friends at university in German city

indicators.note: a piece placed in something sits within its letters rather than being added at either end

parts.note: Ulm stands on the Danube in southern Germany, and these three letters open up after the second
Sir Tim Berners-Lee invented the web, and 'for friends' asks for the first name rather than the surname
the little word is taken at face value, two letters lifted from the clue
U is the standard abbreviation for university

explanation.walkthrough: The surface promises Silicon Valley and student days; every one of those words is really a separate scrap of letters, and all of them end up inside the city.
explanation.definitionFit: Pressing demand -> ULTIMATUM: a final demand with a deadline and a threat behind it, so 'pressing' carries the time limit.

clue.text: Pull out with no win or lose then

parts.note: the word is used as itself, four letters straight from the clue
a match that is neither won nor lost has been drawn

explanation.walkthrough: 'No win or lose' reads as a run of bad luck at the bookmaker's; in the wordplay it is the sporting result that is neither one nor the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Pull out -> WITHDRAW: both mean quitting something you had entered, a race or a deal, rather than physically extracting anything.

clue.text: See red perhaps more than once, beginning to struggle with tension inside

indicators.note: inside means the tension letter is placed within the other word

parts.note: red is one example of wine, and more than once makes it plural, wines
T is the symbol for tension in physics

indicators.note: beginning to means only the first letter of the next word

parts.note: its first letter is used

explanation.surface: Someone sees red again and again, starting to struggle as tension builds within.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See red' looks like the idiom for getting angry, but 'See' alone is the definition and 'red' is a wine.
explanation.definitionFit: To witness something is to see it happen, as an onlooker does.

clue.text: What Heathrow wants: less control, neither left or right-wing policies

indicators.note: less means without, so these letters are taken out

parts.note: Heathrow, London's main airport, has long sought a third runway
to run a business is to control it

explanation.surface: A political jibe: Heathrow wants less regulation, and its politics are neither left nor right.
explanation.walkthrough: The Third Way is the centrist politics associated with Tony Blair and Bill Clinton in the 1990s.
explanation.definitionFit: The Third Way was a centrist political approach meant to sit between traditional left and right.

clue.text: Artist's conflict with Picasso surreal ultimately

parts.note: an armed conflict between states is a war

indicators.note: what comes ultimately comes at the very end, so each word gives up only its final letter

parts.note: the last letters of these three words, in the order the clue sets them down

explanation.walkthrough: Picasso and 'surreal' point at the wrong movement entirely; both are there for their final letters and neither painter is wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: Artist -> WARHOL: definition by example, one artist among thousands, the Pop Art printmaker of the soup tins and the silkscreened film stars.

clue.text: Love Austria being ahead of Germany or Spain

indicators.note: to be ahead of something is to come before it, which fixes the order these pieces are laid in

parts.note: A is Austria's international vehicle code, the oval sticker on the back of a car
D for Deutschland is Germany's international vehicle code
the conjunction is used as itself, two letters from the clue
E for Espana is Spain's international vehicle code

explanation.walkthrough: Three country codes in a row with one plain word between them: these are the letters a driver sees on number plates all over Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: Love -> ADORE: the strong end of the verb, worship rather than mere fondness, and it substitutes straight into 'I love this'.

clue.text: English composer avoiding a river in Moray town

indicators.note: avoiding means keeping away from, so these letters are left out

parts.note: Sir Edward Elgar was the English composer of the Enigma Variations
R is the map abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: An English composer keeps clear of a river in a Scottish town.
explanation.walkthrough: Moray is a council area in north-east Scotland; Elgin is its main town.
explanation.definitionFit: Elgin is a historic town in Moray, in the north-east of Scotland.

clue.text: Husband with dashing looks initially wandering in mountainous area

indicators.note: wandering letters stray from their places, so they are rearranged
takes the opening letter of looks

explanation.surface: A husband with dashing looks roams across a mountain region.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dashing looks' reads as handsome, but dashing is the fodder and looks gives only L.
explanation.definitionFit: The Highlands are the mountainous region of northern Scotland, and generally any upland terrain.

clue.text: Extremely ambitious area including India?

indicators.note: to include something is to hold it within you, so the letter goes inside rather than alongside
the extremes of a word are the letters at its two ends, so everything between them is left out

parts.note: the two outermost letters of ambitious, first and last
a is the abbreviation for area, the one a geometry formula uses
India is I in the NATO alphabet that radio operators spell with

explanation.walkthrough: 'Area' and 'India' each do two jobs at once, defining and handing over a letter; that double duty is what makes four letters this hard.
explanation.definitionFit: area including India? -> ASIA: definition by example, and the question mark admits that naming one country only points at the continent holding it.

clue.text: See 11
British PM and his majesty live in dark times — this may brighten up the sky

definitions.text: this may brighten up the sky
definitions.note: The definition treats the display as one thing while the answer is plural in form: the lights are only ever spoken of together.

indicators.note: one thing set in another sits inside it, so the single letter is buried in the longer word

parts.note: Lord North was prime minister from 1770 to 1782, the one who lost the American colonies
ER is Edwardus Rex, the Latin cypher of a King Edward
the dark hours are nights, and the word opens up after its first letter
L marks the live wire in household wiring, the brown one

explanation.walkthrough: 'PM' invites a modern prime minister and gets a Georgian one; 'his majesty' wants a king's Latin cypher rather than any living monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: this may brighten up the sky -> NORTHERN LIGHTS: the aurora borealis, green curtains of light that hang over high latitudes on a clear winter night.

clue.text: Deceived, Iran's in a fight with everyone which is sort of borderline?

parts.note: had means deceived or tricked, as in 'you've been had'

indicators.note: in a fight suggests the letters are scrambled, as in a brawl

parts.note: taken as written, without the apostrophe
all means everyone

explanation.surface: Iran has been tricked into a war with everyone over a disputed frontier.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the definition is playful: the answer is a literal border.
explanation.definitionFit: Hadrian's Wall is the Roman wall across northern England that marked the empire's frontier, a border line.

clue.text: See 12
England striker talked about after Colombia initially criticised life of luxury here

definitions.note: The definition describes what the place offers rather than naming a place; 'here' is the word that tells you a location is wanted.

indicators.note: a name that is talked about is heard rather than read, so what counts is the sound and not the spelling

parts.note: CO is Colombia's two-letter country code, the one on its web addresses

indicators.note: what comes after something follows it, so this piece is written second in a down entry
the initial of a word is the letter it opens with, and only that letter is taken

parts.note: the opening letter of criticised
Harry Kane is England's record goalscorer, and this spelling of the sound ends the way campaign does

explanation.walkthrough: The spelling is the joke: -AIGNE says 'ayn', exactly as it does in campaign and champagne, so a footballer's name comes out looking medieval.
explanation.definitionFit: life of luxury here -> COCKAIGNE: the imaginary land of plenty in medieval poetry, where roast birds fly into your mouth and nobody works.

clue.text: Mostly better to keep hostilities away from the centre

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it within, so one word shuts around another

parts.note: to better a rival is to outdo them, and the last letter is not wanted
open hostilities between countries are war

explanation.walkthrough: Read as English the clue is about keeping a fight at arm's length; read as wordplay it insists on shutting one in. That reversal is the joke.
explanation.definitionFit: away from the centre -> OUTWARD: the word for motion heading out from a middle point, as in an outward journey or an outward flow.

clue.text: New SEAT oddly lacking airbag — it's designed to deliberately make you angry

definitions.text: it's designed to deliberately make you angry

indicators.note: a new version of something is remade, so these letters are reordered
SEAT without its odd-numbered letters keeps only the second and fourth

explanation.surface: A new Seat car without an airbag is enough to make anyone furious.
explanation.walkthrough: SEAT is a Spanish car maker. Without its odd letters it leaves ET, and ET plus AIRBAG is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Rage bait is online content crafted to provoke anger so that people engage with it.

clue.text: Deranged Trump's latest 'victory': having Venezuela's leader removed for one from Europe

indicators.note: deranged means disordered, so these letters are put in a different order
latest means the last letter of the word

parts.note: the name Trump, whose final letter is taken

indicators.note: removed means this letter is taken out of the word

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: leader means the first letter of the word

parts.note: its first letter is used

explanation.surface: A satirical headline about Trump claiming victory after Venezuela's leader is ousted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trump's latest' is the last letter of the name itself, not of the possessive.
explanation.definitionFit: A Cypriot is a native of Cyprus, a member state of the European Union.

clue.text: Something unusual like bloody chicken

parts.note: a steak cooked rare is still red in the middle
a chicken is one kind of bird

explanation.walkthrough: Both halves come off the same dinner plate, the cooking of the meat and the creature it came from, which is why the clue reads as one phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unusual -> RARE BIRD: an idiom for a person or thing seldom met with, translated straight from the Latin rara avis.

clue.text: Non-theoretical program spread fake news?

parts.note: a program on a phone is an app
whoever spread fake news lied

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark is doing real work: 'spread fake news' is a loose gloss for the second chunk rather than a dictionary synonym for it.
explanation.definitionFit: Non-theoretical -> APPLIED: applied maths and applied science put theory to work on real problems, the other half of the pure-versus-applied split.

clue.text: Very good to receive money for something that is breathtaking

indicators.note: to receive a thing is to take it in, so the letter arrives inside rather than beside

parts.note: so means very, as in 'so good'
G is the standard abbreviation for good, as on a school report
M stands for a million in sums of money, as in a £5m transfer

explanation.walkthrough: 'Breathtaking' is a compliment everywhere except here, where the definition means it literally: air you would rather not breathe.
explanation.definitionFit: something that is breathtaking -> SMOG: the literal reading of the word, a choking mix of smoke and fog that makes breathing hard.

clue.text: Bit of mango fruit topped for later

indicators.note: bit of here means just the first letter of the word

parts.note: its first letter is used

indicators.note: topped means having its top taken off; in a down clue the top is the first letter

parts.note: a banana is a fruit
the first letter removed

explanation.surface: A piece of mango and some fruit with the top cut off are saved for later.
explanation.definitionFit: Mañana is Spanish for tomorrow, used in English to mean at some later time.

clue.text: Parking space was revealed in Welsh town

parts.note: P is the letter on the road sign and the gearstick for parking
an em is a printer's space, the width of a capital M
a story that was revealed broke, as in the news broke overnight

explanation.walkthrough: 'Parking space' is one idea in the surface and two separate abbreviations in the parse. EM is the typesetter's unit and is worth keeping.
explanation.definitionFit: Welsh town -> PEMBROKE: the small town round a Norman castle in the far south-west of Wales, which gives Pembrokeshire its name.

clue.text: Every now and then Emmanuel gets badly hurt

indicators.note: what happens every now and then happens at intervals, so the letters are picked at every second step

parts.note: the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters of the name, read in order

explanation.walkthrough: A long name hides its alternate letters well: count them off in pairs rather than trying to read anything out of the word itself.
explanation.definitionFit: badly hurt -> MAUL: what a bear or a dog does to a person, tearing and battering rather than inflicting one clean injury.

clue.text: One of seven slightly intoxicated

definitions.meaning: Snow White's seven dwarfs are each named for a mood or a habit, and this is the cheerful one
two drinks leave you merry rather than drunk, and English has a mild word for that state

explanation.walkthrough: Four words, no wordplay, and the join is invisible because a dwarf's name and a state of mind are the same word in the same tone.
explanation.definitionFit: One of seven -> HAPPY: definition by example, one dwarf out of Snow White's seven; slightly intoxicated -> HAPPY, the tipsy sense, merry after a drink.

clue.text: At first hungry maneater beheaded an enemy of Rome

indicators.note: at first means the opening letter of the word

parts.note: its first letter is used

indicators.note: beheaded means the first letter is cut off

parts.note: a cannibal eats human flesh
the first letter removed

explanation.surface: A starving man-eater has his head cut off by a foe of ancient Rome.
explanation.definitionFit: Hannibal was the Carthaginian general who crossed the Alps to fight Rome in the Second Punic War.

clue.text: Capital of Campania is not in part of England but somewhere in Italy

indicators.note: is not in means this letter is absent from the word

parts.note: Cumbria is a county in north-west England, home of the Lake District

indicators.note: capital of means the first, capital letter of the word

parts.note: its first letter is used

explanation.surface: A travel note: Campania's capital is in Italy, not an English county.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' suggests Naples, the capital city of Campania, but it means the initial letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Umbria is a region of central Italy, home to Perugia and Assisi.

clue.text: Type of pasta mostly found in lively Siena, a feature of Italy

indicators.note: found in means located inside the other letters
lively means animated, so the letters are stirred into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: mostly means losing the last letter

parts.note: penne is a type of tube-shaped pasta
the last letter removed

explanation.surface: A kind of pasta is mostly eaten in bustling Siena, a typical sight in Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: The Apennines are the mountain range running down the length of the Italian peninsula, a major landmark.

clue.text: Fashion that would be causing great sadness if displayed during hearing

indicators.note: if displayed during describes the answer set inside another word, so taking that word's letters away leaves the answer

parts.note: heartrending means causing great sorrow
taken as written

explanation.surface: A trend is said to cause grief if it is shown off at a court hearing.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue works backwards: 'if displayed during' pictures the answer sitting inside the last word, which would make a word meaning causing great sadness, so that word minus the last word's letters is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A trend is a general direction of change, especially a style in fashion that is popular at the moment.
